inputs.original_text: The Punjab and Haryana High Court has ruled that anticipatory bail cannot be cancelled merely on the ground of non-recovery of stolen articles or the seriousness of allegations. Justice Sumeet Goel ruled that cancellation required clear proof of misuse of liberty or supervening circumstances. Dismissing a plea seeking cancellation of pre-arrest bail in a house [...]
inputs.modified_text: The Punjab and Haryana High Court is right that bail should not be revoked on suspicion alone. But bail is not a clean bill of health, and serious allegations involving stolen property should not be waved away either. The burden is on investigators to build a solid case and show any misuse of liberty; courts must apply that standard consistently. A justice system that protects the accused while taking public safety and victims seriously is essential to public trust.
